description: gosvc fixture: a Go shipment microservice (RPC-style handlers with status-code mapping, bounded connection pool, rolling-window circuit breaker, environment config loading, structured JSON logging, at-least-once broker consumer loop). Tasks are written as a developer would phrase the problem, avoiding the identifier names so the corpus measures semantic retrieval.

cases.task: take a dependency out of rotation when it starts failing a large share of calls, not only when it fails several times back to back
after we have stopped calling something for a while, let a couple of requests through to find out whether it came back
a caller giving up on its own deadline says nothing about how healthy the downstream is, so it should not be held against it
never open more simultaneous connections than we configured, no matter how many goroutines pile in at once, and give up cleanly when the caller's deadline passes while waiting
throw away connections that have been sitting unused for a long time because a firewall has probably already forgotten about them
find out that a socket died quietly during a background sweep instead of letting a customer request discover it
refuse to boot with a precise message when a mandatory setting was never supplied to the container
keep the password out of the connection string we print in the start-up banner
the same event arriving twice from the broker must leave the record in the right state instead of double-applying the change
a record that can never be parsed should be set aside after a bounded number of attempts rather than blocking its partition forever
wait a little longer before each redelivery, but stop growing the wait once it gets silly
avoid a round trip to the broker for every single record by acknowledging our position on a timer instead
answer the caller with a code that tells their client library whether trying again is worth it or whether they must re-read and redo the change
turn away an identifier that is blank, absurdly long, or full of characters that have no business in a key
stop two workers handling the same event from both writing their version of the row
write a whole flush of records in one statement instead of paying a round trip per row
emit one machine-parsable object per line with a clock reading and severity so the log shipper does not need a pattern to index it
give the background loops a bounded window to finish what they are holding when the container is asked to stop
